concepts.definition: The Elm Architecture process model consists of runtime-held typed State; a typed Msg algebra naming every user or system action; pure Update : (Msg, State) → (State, Cmd); pure View : State → ViewTree with identical output for identical state; and typed Cmd/Sub descriptions of scheduled effects and external subscriptions interpreted at the runtime's effect membrane. grounding.quote:
Every admitted constraint evaluation returns the shared
[result record](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra) on its exact subject, basis and
predicate. All five core verdicts are available when evaluating an in-domain
subject. A request outside that domain returns `out_of_frame` at the invocation
boundary; it is not forged into an in-domain judgment. Performance and effect state remain separate
coordinates. An omitted or unperformed evaluation is never a positive result.

The judgment decisions below are domain refinements. `satisfied` maps to the
positive decision, which is first in each row; `invalid_basis` maps only to
`invalid_basis`. The constraint table fixes other mappings. Keep the original
decision, constraint predicate, evidence, residuals and stop in the shared
return. The table does not define a second aggregation or result algebra.

constraints.statement: The closed constraint kinds are identity_dependency_acyclic, occurrence_causation_acyclic, event_causation_acyclic, occurrence_seed_complete, relation_claim_admissible, semantic_cut_complete, pre_effect_current, operation_grant_contains_effect, event_scope_compatible, frontier_complete and transition_subject_complete. Closed judgment kinds are model_validation, occurrence_admission, event_admission, claim_admission, semantic_cut_admission, effect_readiness, transition_evaluation and frontier_projection. Closed residual kinds are unobserved_subject_state, partial_effect, unresolved_cause, unresolved_scope, competing_lineage, stale_frontier, stale_currentness and unobserved_external_mutation. Closed stop kinds are hold, gap, refusal, invalid_basis, out_of_scope and partial_effect. Every admitted evaluation returns the shared result on exact subject, basis and predicate; all five core verdicts remain available in-domain. Out-of-domain invocation returns out_of_frame rather than a fabricated judgment. Performance and effects remain separate; omission or nonperformance is never positive. Decisions refine the shared algebra: satisfied maps to each domain's first positive decision; invalid_basis maps only to invalid_basis; original decision, predicate, evidence, residuals and stop remain. Inherited judgments retain unchanged subject id/digest, evaluator, authority, evidence, provenance and decision; applicable stops/residuals come from the judgment kind, not prose inference. Sigma_occurrence.FunctorKind contains only exact b_ac references to F_D, F_P and F_H and changes none of their laws.
constraints.uncertainty: The imported shared result algebra and b_ac definitions are not supplied in full.

conditions: A judgment of the named kind is being described.

grounding.quote:
| `model_validation` | `OccurrenceModelSubject` | `valid`, `hold`, `refused`, `invalid_basis` | exact model id/digest, profile basis, and typed graph populations | refusal or invalid basis; unresolved refs retain `gap` until repaired |
| `occurrence_admission` | `Occurrence` | `admitted`, `hold`, `refused`, `invalid_basis` | exact occurrence id/digest and resolved pre-existing seed inputs | missing seed retains `hold` plus `unresolved_cause`; re-enter with a new complete occurrence candidate |
| `event_admission` | `FrameworkEvent` | `admitted`, `hold`, `refused`, `invalid_basis`, `out_of_scope` | exact event id/digest, payload digest, scope authority, and source frontier | unresolved scope retains `hold` plus `unresolved_scope`; incompatible scope refuses |
| `claim_admission` | `RelationClaim` | `admitted`, `hold`, `refused`, `invalid_basis` | exact claim id/digest, endpoints, qualifiers, claimant authority, and current source frontier | unresolved cause retains `hold` plus `unresolved_cause`; established staleness falsifies admission while retaining `hold` plus `stale_frontier`; re-enter with a new claim over the current frontier |
| `semantic_cut_admission` | `SemanticAdmissionCut` | `admitted`, `hold`, `refused`, `invalid_basis` | exact seven-member cut and source/successor frontier equality | conjoin claim/event judgments and declared cut joins; missing, held or unauthenticated judgment support retains `hold` plus `unresolved_cause`, naming its slot; established staleness falsifies admission while retaining `hold` plus `stale_frontier`; re-entry follows the unchanged-subject rule below |
| `effect_readiness` | `EffectSubject` | `ready`, `stale`, `unauthorized`, `hold`, `invalid_basis` | exact pre-observation, invocation, operation, grant, territory, and invalidation state | stale yields `hold` plus `stale_currentness` and re-observation; unauthorized yields `refusal` and no dispatch |
| `transition_evaluation` | `TransitionSubject` | `satisfied`, `falsified`, `partial`, `indeterminate`, `refused`, `invalid_basis` | exact pre/post observations, intended outcome, disposition, and bounded effect evidence | partial yields `partial_effect`; indeterminate retains `hold` plus a declared residual; refused yields `refusal` |
| `frontier_projection` | `Projection` | `admitted`, `hold`, `gap`, `refused`, `invalid_basis` | exact projection/frontier ids and digests, complete members, basis, precedence law, boundary, and residuals | stale frontier retains `hold` plus `stale_frontier`; unresolved lineage retains `gap`; re-enter with a new projection |

constraints.statement: model_validation assesses OccurrenceModelSubject with decisions valid/hold/refused/invalid_basis, exact model id/digest, profile basis and typed graph populations; unresolved references retain gap until repair. occurrence_admission assesses Occurrence with admitted/hold/refused/invalid_basis, exact id/digest and resolved pre-existing seeds; a missing seed retains hold and unresolved_cause and requires a new complete candidate. event_admission assesses FrameworkEvent with admitted/hold/refused/invalid_basis/out_of_scope, exact event/payload digests, scope authority and source frontier; unknown scope retains hold/unresolved_scope, incompatible scope refuses. claim_admission assesses RelationClaim with admitted/hold/refused/invalid_basis, exact id/digest, endpoints, qualifiers, claimant authority and current frontier; unknown cause retains hold/unresolved_cause, established staleness falsifies admission with hold/stale_frontier and a new current-frontier claim. semantic_cut_admission uses admitted/hold/refused/invalid_basis, the exact seven-member cut and frontier equalities, conjoining claim/event support and declared joins; missing, held or unauthenticated support retains hold/unresolved_cause naming the slot, while established staleness falsifies with hold/stale_frontier. effect_readiness assesses EffectSubject with ready/stale/unauthorized/hold/invalid_basis and exact pre-observation, invocation, operation, grant, territory and invalidation; stale requires hold/stale_currentness and re-observation, unauthorized requires refusal and no dispatch. transition_evaluation assesses TransitionSubject with satisfied/falsified/partial/indeterminate/refused/invalid_basis, exact pre/post observations, intended outcome, disposition and bounded evidence; partial retains partial_effect, indeterminate hold plus a declared residual, refused refusal. frontier_projection assesses Projection with admitted/hold/gap/refused/invalid_basis, exact projection/frontier identities and digests, complete members, basis, precedence, boundary and residuals; staleness retains hold/stale_frontier, unresolved lineage gap, and re-entry constructs a new projection.

grounding.quote:
Source-frontier currentness is a material join of claim admission, cut
admission and frontier projection. Established staleness falsifies that exact
predicate; its `hold` decision with cause `stale_frontier` prevents use and
requires reconstruction. Unknown currentness is indeterminate. The word
`hold` alone decides neither case. A missing material scope or capability on
an in-domain subject retains core `out_of_frame`, stop `out_of_scope` and
`unresolved_cause` naming the missing relation. Its decision is `hold`, or
`indeterminate` for `transition_evaluation`, whose domain has no `hold` value.
Re-enter with a capable frame under the original subject/basis or retain the
stop. These diagnostic rules apply to every judgment kind without adding a
second verdict domain.

constraints.statement: valid/admitted/ready satisfy only their validation/admission/readiness predicates and establish no external intended outcome. hold/gap/indeterminate retain indeterminate when decisive evidence is missing; demonstrated false predicates remain falsified despite their mapped refused/stale/unauthorized/out_of_scope/established-staleness hold decisions. event_scope_compatible falsification gives decision out_of_scope, distinct from invocation-boundary out_of_frame. transition_evaluation binds the exact intended-outcome predicate and declared observations: demonstrated non-fulfilment is falsified; partial with reason unfulfilled maps to falsified, partial with reason unknown maps to indeterminate; absent required reason/support remains indeterminate without fabricated completion or erased counterevidence. These are reason cases, not new kinds. Preserve partial observations and cause regardless of verdict; outcome failure does not imply no effect. Source-frontier currentness materially joins claim admission, cut admission and projection: known stale means falsified, hold/stale_frontier, no use and reconstruction; unknown means indeterminate. Missing material scope/capability in-domain yields core out_of_frame, stop out_of_scope and unresolved_cause naming the relation, with hold except transition_evaluation uses indeterminate. Re-entry needs a capable frame on the original subject/basis or the stop persists.

exceptions: Established stale-frontier falsification keeps hold/stale_frontier instead of the usual refused/refusal mapping for claim, cut and frontier constraints.

grounding.quote:
| `identity_dependency_acyclic` | `OccurrenceModelSubject` | `model_validation` | `refused` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unresolved_cause` |
| `occurrence_causation_acyclic` | `OccurrenceModelSubject` | `model_validation` | `refused` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unresolved_cause` |
| `event_causation_acyclic` | `OccurrenceModelSubject` | `model_validation` | `refused` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unresolved_cause` |
| `occurrence_seed_complete` | `Occurrence` | `occurrence_admission` | `refused` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unresolved_cause` |

| `semantic_cut_complete` | `SemanticAdmissionCut` | `semantic_cut_admission` | `refused` plus `refusal`; established stale frontier retains `hold` plus `stale_frontier` | `hold` plus `unresolved_cause` naming the undecided slot or join |
| `pre_effect_current` | `EffectSubject` | `effect_readiness` | `stale` plus `hold` and `stale_currentness` | `hold` plus `stale_currentness` |
| `operation_grant_contains_effect` | `EffectSubject` | `effect_readiness` | `unauthorized` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unobserved_subject_state` |
| `event_scope_compatible` | `FrameworkEvent` | `event_admission` | `out_of_scope` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unresolved_scope` |
| `frontier_complete` | `Projection` | `frontier_projection` | `refused` plus `refusal`; established stale frontier retains `hold` plus `stale_frontier` | `hold` plus `unresolved_cause` |

constraints.statement: The three acyclicity constraints use model_validation on OccurrenceModelSubject; occurrence_seed_complete uses occurrence_admission on Occurrence; relation_claim_admissible uses claim_admission on RelationClaim; semantic_cut_complete uses semantic_cut_admission on SemanticAdmissionCut; frontier_complete uses frontier_projection on Projection. Their ordinary falsified mapping is refused/refusal and indeterminate mapping hold/unresolved_cause; cut uncertainty names the slot or join. pre_effect_current uses effect_readiness on EffectSubject: false → stale with hold/stale_currentness; unknown → hold/stale_currentness. operation_grant_contains_effect on that subject/judgment: false → unauthorized/refusal; unknown → hold/unobserved_subject_state. event_scope_compatible uses event_admission on FrameworkEvent: false → out_of_scope/refusal; unknown → hold/unresolved_scope. transition_subject_complete uses transition_evaluation on TransitionSubject: false → refused/refusal; unknown → indeterminate/unobserved_subject_state. Completeness is a prerequisite, not the outcome predicate: proven incompleteness preserves its counterexample and refused decision, while an outcome evaluation unable to use it is invalid_basis; merely unacquired information leaves outcome indeterminate/unobserved_subject_state. Neither proves outcome failure or no effect; independently admissible outcome counterevidence retains its own predicate, valid basis and citations. Residual re-entry is fixed: unobserved_subject_state on SubjectBinding requires bounded observation or retained hold; partial_effect on EffectInvocation requires post-observation and explicit disposition; unresolved_cause requires the named missing authority/evidence/judgment/capability, then unchanged-subject reevaluation where applicable or a successor; unresolved_scope on FrameworkEvent requires lawful scope or refusal; competing_lineage on EventFrontier requires authorized frontier_projection; stale_frontier requires a new claim/cut/projection over the exact current frontier, never in-place rewriting; stale_currentness requires re-observation and re-judgment before effect; unobserved_external_mutation on SubjectBinding requires observation or explicit material unknown.

grounding.quote:
Post-effect observations, effect evidence, judgments, admitted events,
timestamps, admission ordinals, and projection results do not enter the seed.
They may point to the occurrence after their own identities exist.

- state transitions are pure reductions over typed messages
- side effects are values described by the reducer and interpreted at a declared effect membrane
- the runtime owns lifecycle; the view does not own continuation

- a published graph function or lawful graph-function composition
- a workorder, job, or runtime command admitted by the product's design
- an ABG event or command boundary where ABG is the runtime authority

grounding.quote:
The reducer is pure. It does not perform I/O, log to side channels, or mutate global state. Effects scheduled by `Cmd` are interpreted by the runtime at the effect membrane (see §6).

View-local ephemera (open/closed flags, hover state, draft input) may be held in implementation-local state cells where the framework provides them, but only when the value is genuinely view-local (not observed by other views, not part of the product's state surface, not consequential after the view unmounts). Product-meaningful state goes through the reducer without exception.

The discipline test for whether state belongs in the reducer or in view-local ephemera: if losing the value on unmount changes the product's behavior or another part of the UI's view, it belongs in the reducer.

constraints.statement: State changes through typed Msg applied by pure Update. Every surface declares State, Msg, Update:(Msg,State)→(State,Cmd), Cmd and applicable Sub. Product-meaningful state always passes through reducer. Local cells are allowed only when other views do not observe the value, it is outside Product state, and it has no consequence after unmount. If losing it changes Product behavior or another UI view, it belongs in reducer.

exceptions: Observed non-start and reversal cases are required where possible under the command contract.

grounding.quote:
Effect returns distinguish each shared effect state the command can produce
as typed `Msg` cases under its contract, including observed non-start and
reversal where applicable. The method result
records the corresponding shared effect state under the single
[effect observation law](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra); it does not replace
the UX domain's message algebra. The command binding relates each qualified
message to that observation boundary and evidence, preserving missing-reason
and unknown cases rather than guessing from a message name. A failed response after dispatch can mean `unknown`
effects, not proof of no mutation. Before a dependent repeat, the declared
recovery command observes the actual owning state. Reconstructed UI context or
an old success message cannot override that observation. This applies
[workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context) without turning
the effect membrane into a second continuation controller.

constraints.statement: Side effects are isolated to a declared membrane interpreting reducer-produced Cmd and returning typed Msg. I/O, external subscriptions and imperative DOM/filesystem/native interop are allowed inside; render code, render helpers and reducer permit none. The membrane interprets one declared Cmd per effect; branching, conditional state derivation and multistep business decisions belong in reducer. A platform effect handler belongs to the membrane only when interpreting a declared Cmd; conditional logic deciding transitions is a violation regardless of handler name. Typed returns distinguish each possible shared effect state and preserve observation boundary/evidence, missing reasons and unknowns without replacing domain Msg algebra. Failed response after dispatch may mean unknown effect, never proof of no mutation. Before a dependent repeat, recovery observes actual owning state; reconstructed UI context/old success cannot override it. Membrane gains no continuation authority.

conditions: The Product publishes typed AssetSurface contracts, or a design-named equivalent is used.
exceptions: A documented action projection is allowed if it introduces no hidden semantic change.
Products without AssetSurface must name an equivalent typed contract and apply the same law.

grounding.quote:
- the UX surface's `State` is derived from `AssetSurface` projections, not from a UX-local re-declaration of the asset shape
- the UX surface's product-truth-changing `Msg` variants map one-to-one to `AssetSurface` action-registry entries or wrap them through a documented projection with no hidden semantic change
- UX-local `Msg` variants are reserved for view-local concerns (open/closed, sort order, filter input)
- selection within the UX surface emits a Context update (or equivalent) consistent with the product's selection contract
- writes from the UX surface go through the `AssetSurface` action registry, not through direct file or service calls

This is the rule that produces strong functional consistency between front-end and back-end: the same typed contract is the ground truth on both sides.

If the product does not publish `AssetSurface` contracts, the design module must
name the equivalent typed contract and apply the same binding law to that
contract. Absence of an admitted contract blocks product-truth-changing UX
actions.

constraints.statement: Bind one or more AssetSurface contracts as data source/action target. State derives from their projections, not local asset redeclarations. Truth-changing Msg maps one-to-one to action registry entries or faithful documented wrappers; local Msg is reserved for local concerns. Selection emits a Product-selection-consistent Context update/equivalent; writes use action registry rather than direct files/services. The same typed contract grounds both ends. Absence of any admitted AssetSurface/equivalent blocks truth-changing actions.
constraints.uncertainty: ODD §11 and concrete Product contracts are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
State transitions flow through declared `Msg` actions interpreted by the reducer. A view does not:

- decide on its own what the next state will be after a user event
- chain multiple state updates locally without emitting them as separate `Msg` values
- carry hidden inter-event state in refs, closures, or module-level variables

If a view appears to need a multi-step local state machine, that state machine belongs in the reducer as part of `State`, with explicit `Msg` transitions between phases. The view becomes a pure projection of which phase it is in.

The discipline test is the **Msg-replay test**: can you replay the view's behavior by replaying its `Msg` log against an empty `State`? If the answer is no, continuation has leaked into the view.

constraints.statement: The source analogizes ODD's ABG-owned continuation and cooperative bounded-step Product to runtime-owned UX continuation. Views cannot decide next state independently, chain updates without separate Msg, or conceal inter-event state in refs/closures/module variables. Multistep machines belong in reducer State with explicit Msg phase transitions, rendered purely by the view. Failure to replay behavior from Msg log against empty State indicates leaked continuation.
constraints.uncertainty: The informal empty-State test and executable initial-fixture requirement are both retained without forcing them into identical initialization semantics.

conditions: A Product UX surface claims method closure.
exceptions: A pure projection-only surface may use a declared no-effect proof with Msg log, final State and empty Cmd sequence.

grounding.quote:
Every product UX surface must carry at least one executable Msg-replay proof for
each product-meaningful interaction family before claiming method closure.

A replay proof includes:

- an initial `State` fixture
- an ordered `Msg` log
- the expected final `State`
- the expected ordered `Cmd` values
- the typed outcome `Msg` values returned by interpreted `Cmd`s, including
  unresolved effects wherever admitted by the interaction contract
- injected deterministic values for time, randomness, generated ids, and
  external payloads

constraints.statement: At least one executable replay proof is required per Product-meaningful interaction family before closure. Include initial State fixture, ordered Msg, expected final State/ordered Cmd, typed command outcomes including contract-admitted unresolved effects, and deterministic time/randomness/ids/external payloads. Correctness cannot depend on unrepresented DOM state; mutable refs/module variables/closures/timers/handler memory; network/files bypassing Msg; or local state affecting Product after unmount/replay. Assessment returns shared result on exact family predicate, preserving original outcome and command/effect trace. Matching expected final state, ordered commands and typed returns under declared conditions satisfies replay, even if a faithfully reproduced unknown-effect Msg leaves effect completion unresolved. Demonstrated state/command mismatch or forbidden dependency falsifies. Unrun proof retains not_performed and cannot satisfy; missing decisive trace is indeterminate; unusable fixture/basis invalid_basis; out-of-domain interaction out_of_frame. Conjoin required families and other closure checks, preserving failures and missing coverage. Empty commands prove no-effect only when contract declares that predicate.

exceptions: A design-named declared membrane mutation, such as an imperative platform handle, is the stated exception to the out-of-render-mutation violation.

grounding.quote:
The view:

- accepts typed input (state, props, context)
- returns a typed view tree
- declares its consumed inputs explicitly
- does not capture mutable state in closures across renders
- does not read from sources outside its declared input

Whether the implementation expresses this as a function, a function component, a template, a server-rendered handler, a signal-derived expression, or another framework-specific shape is a stack decision recorded in the design module. The constitutional rule is the function signature `State → ViewTree` and the absence of side effects in the body.

A view that depends on out-of-render mutation (e.g., a ref written from inside an effect handler and read during render) is a method violation under §6 unless the mutation is part of the declared effect membrane (e.g., a platform handle for imperative interop already named in the design module).

constraints.statement: View is pure typed State→ViewTree, accepts typed state/props/context, explicitly declares consumed inputs, returns typed tree, captures no mutable cross-render closures and reads no undeclared source. Its framework expression is a recorded stack choice; the body remains effect-free. Dependence on out-of-render mutation violates the method except for the stated declared-membrane case.

exceptions: Local draft/sort/filter types are allowed for local concerns without shadowing back-end types.

grounding.quote:
Runtime validation is mandatory at every untrusted or out-of-process seam:

- HTTP or RPC responses
- MCP payloads
- file-loaded records
- websocket or event-stream messages
- agent or worker outputs
- URL, storage, clipboard, or browser integration payloads

The project uses a typed-schema mechanism so the same type definition is the
source of both compile-time types and runtime validators. The mechanism choice
is project-local. Compile-time TypeScript alone is not sufficient at these
seams.

UX-local types are allowed for view-local concerns: form input draft state, sort order enums, filter strings. UX-local types do not shadow back-end types.

constraints.statement: UX imports back-end shapes from the shared front/back contract module instead of redeclaring them. Every untrusted or out-of-process seam requires runtime validation, including HTTP/RPC, MCP, file records, websocket/events, agents/workers and URL/storage/clipboard/browser integrations. One type definition generates compile-time types and validators through a project-chosen typed-schema mechanism; TypeScript alone is insufficient. Local types cannot shadow shared types.

conditions: A surface publicly exposes a Product capability.
exceptions: Internal-only debug surfaces may omit accessibility when the design module records the exemption.

grounding.quote:
A UX surface that is the public face of a product capability declares:

- semantic structure (heading levels, landmarks, lists, or platform-equivalent affordances)
- keyboard or platform-equivalent navigability for every action that has a pointer interaction
- focus management on dynamic content changes
- accessibility annotations for any custom interactive element that lacks a native semantic equivalent
- color contrast at the project's declared accessibility standard (WCAG AA is the recommended default for web)

Accessibility is not optional for product capabilities. It is optional for internal-only debug surfaces; the design module records the exemption.

This section is intentionally minimal. Projects with stricter accessibility obligations (regulated industry, public-sector procurement) author a project-local accessibility refinement and cite it from their design modules.

constraints.statement: Public capability surfaces declare semantic/platform-equivalent structure; keyboard/platform-equivalent access to every pointer action; dynamic focus management; annotations for custom interactions without native semantics; and contrast at the declared standard. WCAG AA is a recommended web default, not an unconditional mandated standard. Accessibility is not optional for Product capabilities. Stricter project obligations require a cited local refinement.

conditions: A project adopts UX_METHOD.
exceptions: Adoption may cover selected UX surfaces, with scope recorded in the design module; default coverage and exemption laws still require interpretation.

grounding.quote:
A project adopts `UX_METHOD.md` by:

1. naming the method in the project's UX-related design modules
2. recording the realization stack choice (per §12) and the justification
3. declaring the Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set and structural carrier
   diagram required by `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md`
4. declaring the `State`, `Msg`, `Update`, `Cmd`, and `Sub` shapes for each UX
   surface in the design module before implementation
5. declaring the `AssetSurface` or equivalent typed-contract bindings (per §7)
   the surface consumes and emits to
6. naming the effect-membrane mechanism (per §6) and the `Cmd` algebra it
   interprets
7. naming the executable Msg-replay proof surface required by §8A
8. naming any §11 accessibility refinement the project requires
9. noting any §9 view-shape or §6 effect-membrane exemptions explicitly

Adoption is per-project. A project may adopt this method only for some UX surfaces (e.g., the production UI but not internal debug tools), with the scope recorded in the design module.

constraints.statement: Adoption names the method in UX design modules, records justified stack choice, declares the required Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set and structural diagram, declares each surface's State/Msg/Update/Cmd/Sub before implementation, declares consumed/emitted AssetSurface/equivalent contracts, names membrane mechanism and interpreted Cmd algebra, names executable replay proof, names required accessibility refinements and explicitly records view-shape/membrane exemptions.
constraints.uncertainty: The upstream carrier-set and diagram law is referenced but not supplied.

conditions: Any default coverage trigger applies.
exceptions: A scaffold/prototype/debug/temporary-proof surface may be exempt only with the complete stated design-module or ticket record.

grounding.quote:
A UX surface is governed by this method by default when any of these are true:

- it is reachable from the product shell
- it is used as proof for a ticket, requirement, design module, release, or
  review
- it can mutate product truth
- it can spawn, attach, resume, or dispatch work
- it can change Context, selection authority, closure, continuation, evidence,
  or provenance

A scaffold, prototype, debug pane, or temporary proof surface may be exempt only
when the design module or ticket records:

- the exemption scope
- the permitted operations
- whether mutation is forbidden or explicitly bounded
- a visible scaffold/debug label where user-facing
- the authoritative surface that will supersede it
- the retirement condition and owning ticket
- the non-closure condition preventing release if the scaffold remains

An exempt scaffold cannot become the production UX by accumulation. It must be
retired, repriced into a governed UX surface, or kept outside product closure.

constraints.statement: Default coverage applies when shell-reachable, used as ticket/requirement/design/release/review proof, capable of Product mutation, work spawn/attach/resume/dispatch, or changes to Context/selection authority/closure/continuation/evidence/provenance. Exemption records scope, permitted operations, mutation prohibition or bounds, visible label when user-facing, authoritative successor, retirement condition and owner ticket, and a non-closure release block while scaffold remains. Accumulation cannot turn exempt scaffold into production UX; retire it, reprice into governed UX or keep it outside Product closure.

conditions: A UX sprint uses compliance escrow under Spec/Ticket methods.
exceptions: Explicit recorded exemptions decide only their named applicability.
Local paydown at sprint close is permitted only for UX-local debt where the governing method permits follow-up.

grounding.quote:
Sprint-close eligibility and product UX method closure are separate predicates.
The former admits local paydown only under its stated policy. The latter
requires its applicable replay and accessibility proof through core conjunction.
A recorded authorised exemption decides only its named applicability; an
unrecorded exemption supplies no such evidence. Closing the sprint establishes
neither discharge of paydown nor method closure.

The sprint may close with explicit local paydown tickets only where the debt is
local to UX realization and the governing method allows follow-up. It may not
close while product-truth carrier gaps, hidden state continuation, or authority
drift remain unclassified.

Method closure for a product UX surface still requires the §8A Msg-replay proof
and §11 accessibility obligations unless an explicit exemption is recorded. The
sprint can defer those obligations during iteration; it cannot erase them.

constraints.statement: UX is the primary escrow use case. Short-window proof deferral is cost optimization when per-change proof cost exceeds expected correction cost and never weakens the process model. Forbidden escrow findings must be recorded and exit by standalone repricing or sprint supersession. Sprint should close when more iteration is costlier or less trustworthy than review; triggers include timebox expiry, too many changed states, obsolete visual evidence, behavior beyond polish and unsafe reviewer uncertainty. Close is a forensic walkthrough of every changed screen/state/Product-meaningful interaction against authority. Ticket Sprint Close Review owns six treatment classes and reason-sensitive assessment/decision bindings. Bind current surface, adopted scope, applicability/exemption evidence and exact obligations to its map; Contract application assesses admissibility/support separately from UX item compliance. Treatment/decision authority cannot replace compliance assessment; preserve failure, uncertainty, performance and effects even under lawful paydown/removal. Sprint-close eligibility differs from Product UX closure. Close does not discharge paydown or establish method closure. Unclassified carrier gaps, hidden continuation or authority drift prohibit close. Product closure still requires applicable replay/accessibility conjunction unless explicitly exempted; deferral erases nothing.
constraints.uncertainty: The six Ticket treatment classes and their complete eligibility map are not supplied.

conditions: Any enumerated failure pattern occurs in a governed surface.
exceptions: Recorded applicable exemptions and equivalent typed-contract provisions retain their stated scope.

grounding.quote:
17. a UX sprint claims closure while deferred proof, accessibility, carrier,
    scaffold, or authority debt remains unclassified or un-ticketed

Any of these is a method violation. Repeated violations are not normalized by usage; they are repaired or the surface is repriced.

constraints.statement: Any of these violates the method: render mutation of state/props/context; Product state in local cells; transition-deciding effect-handler logic; view-resident multistep machines; mutable-ref reads outside declared membrane; local shadow/redeclaration of backend types; direct file/network selection/action writes bypassing action contracts; unrecorded view exemption; omitted public accessibility without recorded exemption; Msg-free two-way binding bypassing reducer; imperative handler logic that should be Cmd; behavior unreplayable from Msg/empty State; truth-changing Msg without admitted carrier; unvalidated external ingress; reachable/mutating/proof scaffold without exemption record; ADR/convention/existing-code weakening; or sprint closure with unclassified or unticketed proof/accessibility/carrier/scaffold/authority debt. Repetition never normalizes violation: repair or reprice.

conditions: A UX surface review is performed.

grounding.quote: A UX surface review under this method should answer:
If any of these cannot be answered, the design module is incomplete.

constraints.statement: Review should answer: State/Msg/Update; Cmd/Sub; bound AssetSurface/equivalents; admitted carriers for truth changes; membrane and interpreted Cmd; provable view purity; executable Msg replay; imported shared types; pre-state validation of all out-of-process payloads; documented view/membrane/accessibility/scaffold/debug exemptions; chosen stack and model preservation; no view continuation under replay; Design Module carrier set/diagram; and, if a sprint was used, classification of every deferred proof/accessibility/carrier/scaffold/authority finding. If any cannot be answered, the design module is incomplete.

grounding.quote:
`UX_METHOD.md` is not:

- a styling guide or design system specification
- a component library
- a brand or visual-identity surface
- a wireframing or prototyping process
- a research method for user studies
- a stack ranking or framework recommendation

Those are valid concerns; they belong in product-local surfaces, not in this constitutional method.

constraints.statement: UX_METHOD is not a styling/design-system specification, component library, brand surface, wireframing/prototyping process, user-study research method or stack/framework ranking. These concerns belong in Product-local surfaces.

conditions: The method covers the UX surface.
exceptions: Explicit bounded scaffold/debug exemptions and permitted visible sprint escrow retain their stated conditions.

grounding.quote:
When adopted, this method is the sole UX realization authority for the covered
surface. Product-truth-changing UX messages must map to admitted product
carriers; the UX layer must not become the hidden constructive carrier. External
payloads are runtime-validated before entering UX state. Scaffolds and debug
surfaces are governed unless explicitly exempted, bounded, and retired. UX
sprints may defer local proof and cleanup only as visible compliance escrow;
close review must classify and pay down the debt before method closure is
claimed.

constraints.statement: The canonical compression reiterates TEA, Design Module refinement, runtime State, typed Msg, pure Update/View, membrane Cmd→Msg, no view continuation and replay discipline. Stack remains justified project choice; realizations are assessed against §§4–10 and absence of §14 failures, without stack ranking. Covered truth-changing messages require admitted carriers, ingress validation is mandatory, scaffold/debug status requires explicit bounds and retirement, and visible escrow may defer local proof/cleanup but debt must be classified and paid down before method closure.

conditions: A Product adopts world-model construction; geometric overlay rules additionally require geometric representation.
exceptions: Linked common methods apply only under their own applicability conditions; the theoretical Design Module relation creates no prerequisite.
Code availability and a comparison population are not themselves prerequisites for ordinary entity-cut admission.

grounding.quote:
These links create
no new prerequisite; the theoretical Design Module relation below remains
non-prerequisite. Where the consuming Product also
selects graph-native realization, [ODD Method](ODD_METHOD.md) retains execution
shape and traversal law while this member retains world-model meaning.
Availability of either method leaves its adoption and operation authority with
the declared owners.

Apply [Contract application](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#contract-application)
to each claim-assurance, entity-cut admission and publication use with its exact
source authority, qualified subject, current evidence, treatment/basis and grant.
Acquisition traces the strongest available source surfaces; code availability
is not a prerequisite. A materialized cut, authorized candidate-class
publication and established statistical claim retain different predicates.

constraints.statement: World Model Method maps Foundations/Transformation Library and common Spec/Identity/Design Module/Ticket/Release surfaces without adding prerequisites. When graph-native realization is also selected, ODD retains execution/traversal and World Model retains semantics; owners retain adoption/operation authority. Assurance, entity admission and publication apply Contract application with exact authority, qualified subject, current evidence, treatment/basis and grant. Distinguish materialization, authorized candidate publication and established statistical claims. Local semantic accounts never replace operational truth; equal labels establish neither identity nor lineage. Entity admission requires eight surfaces/support with proportional evidence altitude; reasoned non-applicability or stated absence may establish explicitness, sparse publication retains ambiguity, stronger boundary claims need stronger discrimination, and no individual discrimination technique is mandatory. Append-only ledgers/publications preserve historical support and currentness. Treatment/composition preserve declared identity, authority, meaning and admitted loss by reference; covariance/adjoint terminology proves no mathematical adjunction or equivalence. Geometric overlays require paired evidence, extraction, held-out verification, null-peer conditions and published fields; evidence concerns the actual treatment, not every possible one. Different spaces have incompatible directions; changed space supersedes overlay without generic translation exception. Statistical promotion is separate from direction publication; companion evidence grants no method authority. Semantic control, probabilistic proposal and deterministic data plane remain distinct and do not mandate graph-native carriers. Publication/supersession first assesses eligibility, then separately the decision predicate on exact candidate/basis/disposition/mandate. Established support may satisfy each; failed requirement or exceeded mandate falsifies its predicate; missing support is indeterminate; invalid basis/interpretation or established scope/capability shortfall gets its corresponding diagnosis. Unresolved treatment retains actual standing including known failure. Publication does not establish statistical closure. Shared result/conjunction applies; lifecycle names, field values and evidence classes are not automatic verdict aliases.
constraints.uncertainty: Several detailed consuming clauses summarized by this section are not supplied.

conditions: Within the selected complete STDO basis and world-model method scope.
exceptions: A consuming Product may declare narrower owned contexts without changing the method context by proximity.

grounding.quote:
The meanings are adopted unchanged for this method scope under the selected
complete STDO basis. Their SPEC owner is retained, and a change to either
context, any cited concept or taxonomy clause, or the selected STDO basis
invalidates the import until reevaluated. `GLOSSARY_GUIDE.md` only locates those
source-owned meanings. No other same-spelled concept is imported by this
declaration. For each import, the source and target concept reference is the
same listed identity; the relation expands applicability into the target
context and mints no alias or new semantic owner.

constraints.statement: World Model Method refines SPEC's general constitution for observing source systems and publishing bounded artifacts, owns urn:stdo:bounded-context:world-model and is primary within that domain. For graph-native world-model Products, ODD governs execution shape/traversal/authoring, while this method governs semantics/publication/composition; they compose. Exactly source-project, product, install and artifact at urn:stdo:concept:recursive-product-taxonomy:<name> are imported from SPEC_METHOD.md#recursive-product-taxonomy and its recursive-product-taxonomy context into world-model context unchanged. SPEC ownership remains; the same identities expand applicability without alias or new owner. Context/concept/taxonomy-clause/basis changes invalidate import until reevaluation. Glossary only locates meanings; no other same-spelled concepts import. Product remains released immutable thing, including possible builder/runtime Product; Install remains stamped workspace instance; Source Project remains mutable next-release workspace; Artifact remains published output; PRODUCT.md remains Source Project definition, not released Product.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete selected basis and source taxonomy clause are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
We allow the world model to become generative only after it is descriptively
grounded.

If these claims do not hold, the work is not genuinely world-model-driven.

constraints.statement: The manifesto commits world-model work to observation before standardization; enacted-semantic comprehension before schema flattening; function-bounded domains; data as contextual evidence; recovery of expert objects/boundaries/states/transitions/treatments/references; materialized governed understanding rather than detached knowledge; conceptual institutional knowledge beyond metadata; semantic grounding of probabilistic reasoning before cross-domain interpretation; qualified names before semantic transformation; treatment/covariance/adjoint interpretation instead of naked field mapping; immutable cuts with explicit supersession; composition preserving local authority; probabilistic overlays with accepted understanding compiled deterministically where volume requires; projections subordinate to the kernel; and descriptive grounding before generation. The source makes these commitments constitutive of world-model-driven work.

exceptions: Generic object references denote the published entity cut unless an explicitly looser candidate/intermediate surface is named.

grounding.quote:
Its primary semantic unit is the published entity cut: an
identity-bearing, evidence-backed, bounded semantic cut projected from the
attribute ledger. Generic references to a "world-model object" are shorthand
for this unit unless the text explicitly names a looser candidate or
intermediate surface.

constraints.statement: A world model is descriptive before generative and has the published entity cut as primary semantic unit. It should expose real objects/context, coherent boundaries, relevant state/transitions, supporting evidence, governing classifications, adjacent reinterpretations, covariance, and what is preserved/changed/aggregated/delayed/lost. It is not a replacement system of record, semantics-erasing monolith, generic catalog entry, copied warehouse or schema registry substituted for comprehension.

conditions: Markov-object constructs or overlays are being characterized.
exceptions: These refinements do not govern entity-cut admissibility.

grounding.quote:
Four findings from the empirical program constrain how the method
treats Markov objects. They are working refinements: the program has
produced candidate evidence for them, not a formal closure. The
method adopts them as the best current reading of the construct.

They constrain the Markov-object construct and overlays built on it.
They are not admissibility conditions for entity cuts, which are
governed by *Entity Cut Construction Law*.

constraints.statement: The source adopts four candidate-evidence working refinements, in the pinned companion's order/meaning, without formal closure: (1) exp 17 supports geometric identity axis over leaky set-valued column boundaries; test identity survival under treatment. (2) Attribute schemas sense/fragment rather than isolate; fixed bases partially align and distribute identity, so published overlays must expose axis as well as profile; schema is evidence, not ontology. (3) exps 15/16 favor invariant semantic core over size: sparse meaningful invariant can be lawful while rich non-invariant cluster is not; more columns confer no objecthood and sparse first publication remains lawful. (4) exp 18 treats identity as mean/DC offset from a null peer rather than dominant variance, excluding principal-component/maximum-variance constructions as identity directions. Later companion revisions do not silently change the pinned reading.
constraints.uncertainty: The empirical companion, experiments and pin are not included.

exceptions: Entity cuts use their own admissibility test and do not inherit Markov candidate status.
Method adoption does not require empirical-program completion.

grounding.quote:
Promotion gate. The experimental result that would promote the
construct from candidate to established is a direction-native
conditional-independence test: given the identity projection,
residual variation along remaining components should be independent
of the target under plausible treatments. That test has been run and
did not meet its predicate, and its multi-layer successor did not
either. The gate stands where it is; it has not been met and must not
be relocated to accommodate the negative result.

This status attaches to the Markov-object construct and to overlays
built on it. A published Markov-object overlay is a candidate-class
overlay of a candidate construct, not a certified blanket of a
formally-established object.

It does not attach to entity cuts. An entity cut is lawful published
truth on its own admissibility test and does not inherit the
construct's candidate status. A candidate entity that has not met
that test is a candidate; a published entity cut is not.

This epistemic status is inherited downstream. Tooling that
materializes Markov-object overlays under this method should default to a
candidate-class publication kind and reserve any formally-closed
publication kind for cuts backed by a real promotion-gate result.

constraints.statement: Markov object remains load-bearing working vocabulary with candidate empirical status; geometric evidence does not establish statistical conditional independence. Claims depending on a formally established blanket remain revisable working commitments. Promotion requires a direction-native test that residual variation, given identity projection, is independent of target under plausible treatments. The source reports both that test and its multilayer successor failed their predicate; the gate remains unmet and may not move to accommodate failure. Published overlays are candidate-class, not certified blankets. Downstream tooling should default to candidate-class and reserve formally closed publication for actual gate-backed cuts. Ordinary admitted entity cuts are lawful on their separate test; unadmitted entity candidates remain candidates.
constraints.uncertainty: Reported experimental outcomes are interpreted as source claims, not independently verified findings.

grounding.quote:
The method should produce world models that are:

- bounded
- inspectable
- challengeable
- evidence-backed
- versioned
- composable
- projection-capable
- machine-reasonable

If the method is working, it should become possible to answer:

- what object is this record evidence of
- what boundary defines that object
- what source evidence supports the claim
- which source is locally authoritative
- what treatment changed the meaning downstream
- what relationship exists between two differently treated objects
- what value list or classification was in force at the time
- why a downstream figure is or is not explainable from upstream reality

constraints.statement: The method should produce bounded, inspectable, challengeable, evidence-backed, versioned, composable, projection-capable, machine-reasonable models. It should enable answers about a record's object/boundary, supporting evidence and local authority, downstream semantic treatment, relations among differently treated objects, temporal classification/value lists, and downstream figures' explanation from upstream reality. These are stated objectives, not automatic evidence of achievement.

conditions: World-model work re-enters or reuses earlier claims.
exceptions: Valid closed claims and bounded evidence refs may be reused without loading every historical ledger entry or resetting sources.

grounding.quote:
Operational truth remains with the systems that enact it.

The world model is a derived semantic layer over those systems. It is not a
replacement operational source.

On re-entry, observe the current source surfaces and check the invalidators of
reused claims under [workspace and context](FOUNDATIONS.md#workspace-and-context).
A prior cut remains an immutable account at its declared basis; it cannot
overrule a contrary current observation. Reacquiring context may reuse valid
closed claims and bounded evidence references without loading every prior
ledger entry or resetting the sources.

constraints.statement: Operational truth remains with enacting source systems. The derived world model cannot replace them. Re-entry observes current sources and checks reused-claim invalidators; immutable prior cuts remain basis-bound accounts and cannot overrule contrary current observation.

grounding.quote:
Data is a trace of constrained function execution.

It is invalid in isolation from context.

constraints.statement: Data is evidence tracing constrained function execution; isolated from context it is invalid as an account of meaning.

conditions: A cross-domain treatment is declared.

grounding.quote:
Cross-domain transformation is not plain structural rewrite.

Every treatment must declare preserved structure, changed meaning, loss,
surplus, and ambiguity.

constraints.statement: Every treatment declares preserved structure, changed meaning, loss, surplus and ambiguity. Cross-domain transformation is semantic, not merely structural rewrite.

grounding.quote:
### Fully Qualified Naming Is Mandatory

Many cross-domain failures are preventable naming collisions.

Fully qualified naming removes aliasing so the remaining hard work is real
semantic transformation.

constraints.statement: Fully qualified naming is mandatory to remove preventable aliasing; resolving naming collisions does not itself perform semantic transformation.

grounding.quote:
Changing code sets, classifications, and value lists are governed temporal
reference artifacts, not static enum decorations.

constraints.statement: Changing code sets, classifications and value lists retain governed temporal-artifact standing rather than static-enum treatment.

grounding.quote:
API contracts and schema contracts are projections over the world model.

They are useful because they publish structure and function. They are not the
highest semantic authority.

constraints.statement: API/schema contracts publish useful structure and function as world-model projections, but are not highest semantic authority.

grounding.quote:
The canonical published entity cut should remain semantic and bounded.

Probability belongs in uncertainty, ranking, anomaly, and alignment overlays,
not in the ontological identity of the published object itself.

That overlay may include:

- correspondence candidates
- confidence and ranking
- ambiguity registers
- anomaly and surprise signals
- candidate mappings or treatment suggestions

The overlay is useful because it lets probabilistic reasoning operate over a
governed semantic substrate rather than over detached strings, schemas, or raw
tables.

But the overlay is not the same thing as published semantic truth.

Accepted semantic treatments, published domain artifacts, and compiled
deterministic execution artifacts remain distinct from probabilistic overlays.

constraints.statement: Canonical entity cuts should remain semantic and bounded. Probability belongs in uncertainty/ranking/anomaly/alignment overlays, not ontological object identity. Overlays may contain correspondence candidates, confidence/ranks, ambiguity registers, anomaly/surprise and mapping/treatment suggestions over governed semantics. They remain distinct from published truth, accepted treatments, artifacts and deterministic compiled execution.

exceptions: Code/rules/configuration are used when available; code availability is never a comprehension prerequisite.

grounding.quote:
Preferred hierarchy:

1. realized system behavior and emitted records or events
2. source code, rules, and configuration when available
3. interfaces and schemas
4. large-scale observational data evidence
5. documentation, catalogs, and operator testimony

Code is a high-fidelity explanatory surface when available.

Realized behavior remains the broader truth surface because some systems are
proprietary, partially visible, or only intelligible through their outputs and
effects.

The method therefore never depends on code availability as a prerequisite for
comprehension.

constraints.statement: Work from strongest available explanatory surfaces with preferred order: realized behavior and emitted records/events; available source code/rules/configuration; interfaces/schemas; large-scale observational evidence; documentation/catalogs/operator testimony. Code is high-fidelity when available, but behavior remains broader for proprietary or partially visible systems. This is a preference hierarchy, not a requirement to possess every tier.

conditions: The Observe stage is undertaken.
exceptions: Code and configuration are conditional on availability.

grounding.quote:
Gather source evidence from the strongest available surfaces:

- runtime behavior
- source records and events
- code and configuration when available
- interfaces and schemas
- docs and metadata

constraints.statement: Observe gathers strongest-available evidence from runtime behavior, records/events, available code/configuration, interfaces/schemas and documentation/metadata.

conditions: The Trace stage is undertaken.

grounding.quote:
Index and locate the source surfaces that may support semantic claims.

Tracing should make it possible to point from a later world-model attribute
claim back to the concrete source span, field, locator, code path, or record
that supports it.

constraints.statement: Trace indexes/locates potentially supporting surfaces and should enable later attribute claims to point back to concrete source spans, fields, locators, code paths or records.

conditions: The Extract stage is undertaken.

grounding.quote:
Produce reviewable intermediate surfaces from traced source objects:

- source inventories
- object candidates
- event and lifecycle candidates
- treatment candidates
- authority candidates
- ambiguity registers

These are not the world model yet.

They are the auditable path toward it.

constraints.statement: Extract produces reviewable inventories, object/event/lifecycle/treatment/authority candidates and ambiguity registers from traced sources. They are auditable intermediate surfaces, not yet the world model.

conditions: The Assure stage assesses a qualified claim.
exceptions: Tolerated ambiguity may remain explicit when admissible evidence reaches the required evidence altitude.

grounding.quote:
Return that exact claim through the shared
[result record](FOUNDATIONS.md#result-algebra), retaining its original
assurance outcome, evidence class and residual ambiguity. The predicate is
"claim C is supported on its declared subject/basis under its stated assurance
rule." Admissible evidence establishing that claim at the required evidence
altitude satisfies it, with tolerated ambiguity explicitly retained.
An observed counterexample is `falsified`; missing decisive support is `indeterminate`.
An unusable basis is `invalid_basis`, and an out-of-domain request is
`out_of_frame`. A proposed claim or an assessment not performed is never
`satisfied` by default. `observed`, `derived`, `interpreted` and `composed`
describe evidence provenance; they are not alternative success values.

constraints.statement: Assure qualifies traced observations by binding declared purpose, interpreted predicate and actual observations. Predictive adequacy differs from required construction outcome: accuracy does not prove construction success and prediction error alone does not prove failure. Distinct accounts/correction follow Bounded construction. Assurance should expose claim, observed/derived/interpreted/composed provenance, support surfaces, aspect-specific authority and remaining ambiguity/missingness. Return exact claim support on declared subject/basis/rule through shared result, retaining original assurance outcome, evidence class and residuals. Adequate admissible evidence satisfies; counterexample falsifies; missing decisive support is indeterminate; unusable basis invalid_basis; out-of-domain out_of_frame. Proposal/nonperformance defaults to no success. Provenance categories are never success aliases.
constraints.uncertainty: Required evidence altitude and imported Bounded construction law are not fully specified here.

conditions: Qualified claims have been accepted.

grounding.quote:
Write the accepted qualified claims into the attribute ledger.

The ledger is append-only. New understanding is recorded as new qualified
claims and later object cuts, not by mutating prior accepted entries in place.

constraints.statement: Ledger records accepted qualified claims append-only. New understanding produces new qualified claims and later cuts; prior accepted entries are never mutated in place.

conditions: The Bound stage is undertaken.

grounding.quote:
Identify bounded contexts and the candidate entities that actually cohere
inside them.

Reject schema-first modeling and vocabulary-cluster modeling.

Define local boundaries in terms of function, authority, state, and adjacency.

constraints.statement: Bound identifies coherent candidate entities within bounded contexts, rejects schema-first and vocabulary-cluster modeling, and defines local boundaries by function, authority, state and adjacency.

conditions: The Materialize stage is undertaken.
exceptions: Sparse first publication is lawful when bounded, distinguishable and evidence-backed.

grounding.quote:
Project entity cuts from the attribute ledger with enough semantic
context for alignment and reasoning.

Sparse first publication is lawful if the object is bounded, distinguishable,
and evidence-backed.

constraints.statement: Materialize projects ledger-backed entity cuts with enough context for alignment and reasoning; sparsity alone does not prohibit first publication under the stated conditions.

conditions: The Relate stage is undertaken.

grounding.quote:
Add treatment surfaces, covariance edges, adjoint mappings, and temporal
reference artifacts.

This is where cross-domain meaning becomes explicit.

constraints.statement: Relate adds treatments, covariance, adjoint interpretation and temporal reference artifacts to make cross-domain meaning explicit.

conditions: The Publish stage is undertaken.
exceptions: Git and filesystem are sufficient publication authority in the low-volume lane.

grounding.quote:
Publish immutable cuts of the published domain artifact.

Do not mutate prior published truth in place.

In the low-volume lane, Git and the filesystem are sufficient as publication
authority.

constraints.statement: Publish immutable domain-artifact cuts without in-place mutation of prior published truth. The low-volume Git/filesystem sufficiency statement does not itself assess a particular publication or grant.

conditions: The Compose stage is undertaken.

grounding.quote:
Stitch published domain artifacts, their fragments, and their published
entity cuts into higher-order world models without erasing local
authority.

Composition is recursive, inspectable, and bounded.

constraints.statement: Compose stitches published artifacts, fragments and entity cuts into higher-order models while retaining local authority; composition remains recursive, inspectable and bounded.

conditions: The Project stage is undertaken.
exceptions: Tests/application scaffolds are outputs where applicable.

grounding.quote:
Emit familiar outputs from the same semantic kernel:

- tables
- schema contracts
- API contracts
- event contracts
- mapping documents
- transformation specifications
- covariant transforms
- tests and application scaffolds where applicable

constraints.statement: Project emits tables, schema/API/event contracts, mapping documents, transformation specifications, covariant transforms and applicable tests/scaffolds from the same semantic kernel.

conditions: An entity cut is published.
exceptions: Geometric discharge applies where a declared representation space exists; elsewhere discharge is semantic under Entity Cut Construction Law.

grounding.quote:
Every published entity cut must be prompt-sufficient for reasoning.

At minimum, the cut should make visible:

- identity
- boundary
- authority
- state
- evidence
- treatment
- covariance
- ambiguity

"Make the effective blanket explicit" means: state the boundary at which the
entity's identity survives reinterpretation, not enumerate a set of member
attribute columns. Attribute schemas are evidence for identity, not identity
itself.

The boundary is interventional, not structural. The test is "does this
identity survive treatment across its adjacent domains?", never "which
attributes are in the member set?"

Where a declared representation space exists, that boundary takes its
geometric form: the low-rank projection along which identity is preserved
under treatment. A Markov-object overlay should then expose both the
distributed attribute evidence and the projection that recovers identity from
it. Outside such a space the same law is discharged semantically, under
*Entity Cut Construction Law*.

constraints.statement: Every published cut must be prompt-sufficient. It should expose at least identity/boundary/authority/state/evidence/treatment/covariance/ambiguity. Explicit blanket means the interventional boundary where identity survives adjacent-domain treatment, never column membership; schemas evidence rather than constitute identity. In a declared geometric space this is a low-rank identity-preserving projection, and overlays should expose distributed evidence plus recovering projection. Outside that space the semantic entity-cut construction law applies.
constraints.uncertainty: The full Entity Cut Construction Law and operational prompt-sufficiency test are absent.

exceptions: One ledger state may support many cuts with differing identities, boundaries and context scopes.

grounding.quote:
The attribute ledger is the accepted semantic record over which the entity cut
is projected. A single ledger state can support many different cuts at
different identities, boundaries, and context scopes; the cut records which
selection was taken, not that the ledger *is* the cut.

Every accepted object attribute should therefore be recoverable through:

- the object cut that contains it
- the attribute-ledger entries that justify it
- the assurance basis that accepted those entries
- the traced source surfaces that support the assurance

No object attribute should exist without ledger support. No ledger entry should
exist without assurance. No assurance should exist without traceable source.

constraints.statement: Materialized entity cuts are builder artifacts, not raw source artifacts. Source retains operational truth; builder observes/comprehends; published cut is canonical object-level world-model truth; downstream projections derive from it. Domain artifacts should be versioned and explicitly superseded. A cut is immutable governed understanding, not a claim that source directly emitted the object. The chain is source→tracing→assurance→ledger→cut. Projection selects bounded identity/boundary over distributed ledger evidence with accepted basis; geometric selection applies only in declared representation space. Cut selection never equates ledger with cut. Every accepted attribute should be recoverable via containing cut, justifying entries, accepting assurance and traced source. No attribute should lack ledger support, no entry assurance, and no assurance source trace.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced construction laws are not supplied in full.

forbidden: Treating precedence ordering of eligible facts as semantic, admission, causal or decision authority.

grounding.quote:
A projection may use a declared precedence coordinate to select current truth.
The coordinate, comparison law, basis, and admitting authority are explicit.
The coordinate orders eligible facts; it does not gain semantic, admission,

forbidden: Inferring rollback from a new occurrence.

grounding.quote:
Snapshotting or rollback may be supplied by a separately authorized
application. This profile neither requires nor forbids it and does not infer
rollback from a new occurrence.

allowed: Project-local stack choice recorded in the design module with a short justification of §4 model preservation.

Any realization preserving §§4–8; examples are non-normative: native reducer runtime, typed reducer plus interpreter, reactive projection behind reducer, or server-derived state with request/response membrane.
forbidden: Negotiating away the constitutional model or ranking frameworks as a method requirement.
View-owned continuation, render effects, mutation outside typed reducer, Msg-bypassing multistep machines, two-way binding without Msg, imperative render DOM mutation, or effect-handler controllers.
Reactive signal mutation outside the reducer.

grounding.quote:
The process model is the Elm Architecture. The implementation stack is the project's choice, recorded in the project's design module.

This mirrors `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` §4 ("Functional Bias Without Language Mandate"). The rule is:

- the **process model** is constitutional and not negotiable
- the **stack** is project-local and free, provided it preserves the model

Any realization that preserves §4–§8 is method-compliant. Examples (non-normative):

What is constitutionally rejected: any realization that lets the view own state continuation, performs side effects in render code, mutates state outside a typed reducer, or carries multi-step view-local state machines that bypass `Msg`. Two-way binding without `Msg` emission, imperative DOM manipulation in render code, and effect-handlers used as controllers are violations regardless of stack.

A project that selects a framework records the choice in its design module along with a short justification of how the framework preserves the §4 process model. The method does not rank frameworks. The method tests realizations against §4–§8.

allowed: Project chooses language, framework/runtime, state-container library if any, effect interpreter, runtime validator if any, and build/bundling/deployment tools; records each choice and brief §4/§6 preservation justification.
forbidden: Using stack preference instead of realization inspection: this section states compliance when §§4–10 hold and §14 failure patterns are absent.

grounding.quote:
The project chooses:

- the language
- the framework or runtime
- the state-container library (if any)
- the effect-interpreter mechanism
- the runtime validator (if any)
- the build, bundling, and deployment toolchain

The project records its choices in the design module along with a short justification of how each choice preserves the §4 Elm process model and the §6 effect-membrane rule.

The method does not rank stacks. It tests realizations. A realization is method-compliant when §4–§10 hold under inspection and the §14 failure patterns are absent.

allowed: During a short qualifying UX sprint, defer screenshots/walkthrough capture, visual review, copy/spacing/density/layout cleanup, accessibility review/remediation, interaction-family replay updates, design wording and changed-state authority-trace cleanup.

forbidden: Escrowing truth-changing Msg without admitted carrier; new/changed AssetSurface or equivalent contracts; meaning-changing navigation/information architecture/selection authority; runtime/governance/closure/continuation/lineage/provenance/evidence semantics; release criteria or method law.
Weakening TEA, hiding a constructive carrier, erasing deferred obligations or equating sprint closure with method closure.

grounding.quote:
A UX sprint may escrow:

- screenshots or walkthrough capture
- visual review
- copy, spacing, density, and layout cleanup
- accessibility review and remediation
- Msg-replay proof updates for product-meaningful interaction families
- design-module wording cleanup
- trace cleanup between changed UX states and governing authority

A UX sprint may not escrow:

- product-truth-changing `Msg` variants that lack an admitted carrier
- new or changed `AssetSurface` contracts or equivalent typed product contracts
- new navigation, information architecture, or selection authority that changes
  product meaning
- runtime, governance, closure, continuation, lineage, provenance, or evidence
  semantics
- release criteria or method law

If one of those appears, the sprint records the finding and the work exits the
UX sprint path through standalone repricing or sprint supersession. The UX layer
must still not become the hidden constructive carrier.

Use the semantic kernel as a tether for probabilistic alignment across domains,
entity cuts, artifacts, and projections.

This stage may produce:

understanding into deterministic executable artifacts.

Examples may include:

- data-movement specifications
- transformation jobs
- high-volume ETL or ELT plans
- deterministic mapping-tool records
- generated implementation artifacts

The important rule is:

- probabilistic correspondence may help comprehension
- accepted semantic understanding governs compilation
- execution at scale should run through deterministic compiled artifacts rather

exceptions: Parent-governed immutability, totality, effect-edge discipline, no-semantic-center and coupling are cited/extended rather than duplicated.

`UX_METHOD.md` refines `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` with the additional rules required when a module realizes a UX surface — render purity, state-transition algebra, effect-membrane discipline, and accessibility minimums — under the Elm Architecture process model.

`UX_METHOD.md` does not duplicate `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md`. Where the parent method already governs (immutability, totality, effect-edge discipline, no-semantic-center, coupling), `UX_METHOD.md` cites and extends it. Where UX has concerns the parent does not address (render lifecycle, browser events, layout, accessibility), `UX_METHOD.md` is authoritative.

SPEC retains constitutional process/re-entry; ODD retains constructive-carrier law; Design Module retains deterministic realization. Governing is true only for the source-declared UX process model.

exceptions: Non-UX modules receive Design Module discipline only.

grounding.quote:
`UX_METHOD.md` composes with the upstream methods on a per-surface basis:

- when a module realizes a UX surface, both `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` and `UX_METHOD.md` apply
- when a module realizes a non-UX surface, only `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` applies
- when an ODD product publishes a projection / query surface that includes UX (`§10` of `ODD_METHOD.md`), `UX_METHOD.md` governs that surface's realization

The composition rule is:

- `ODD_METHOD.md` answers what graph-native shape the product takes
- `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` answers what realization discipline the modules follow
- `UX_METHOD.md` answers what additional discipline UX surfaces follow

relations.meaning: UX Method imposes its Elm process discipline per UX surface alongside Design Module law; upstream graph shape and general realization roles remain separate.

conditions: UX is realized over a Product with world-model state.
exceptions: Non-UX design modules use Design Module Method only and ignore UX Method.

grounding.quote:
- `SPEC_METHOD.md` governs constitutional process, authority flow, repricing, and migration law.
- `ODD_METHOD.md` governs graph-native constructive carrier law. UX surfaces are projection / query surfaces under §10 of that method.
- `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` governs deterministic realization discipline at the module level. `UX_METHOD.md` refines it for UX modules.
- `TICKET_METHOD.md` governs ticket and sprint lifecycle. UX work may use sprint compliance escrow under §13B when the sprint boundary makes deferred proof visible, bounded, and payable.
- `WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md` governs world-model semantic law for products that have a world-model dimension. UX surfaces over world-model state still bind through `AssetSurface` (or equivalent) per §7.

A UX-touching design module reads `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` plus `UX_METHOD.md`. A non-UX design module reads `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` only and ignores this surface.

relations.meaning: UX Method composes with World Model semantic law while UX binds through AssetSurface/equivalent. Neither method gains the other's authority from this relation. SPEC owns process/authority/repricing/migration; ODD carrier shape; Design Module realization; Ticket lifecycle and visible bounded payable escrow.

conditions: World-model construction under the same selected complete STDO release containing both source and target clauses.
Workspace is configured for the builder application and owns source inputs, settings and publication lane.
exceptions: No inverse, equivalence or claim that every Source Project is a Builder Project.
General Source Projects outside the narrower configuration are excluded; installed builder Product or Install cannot substitute.
relations.meaning: Source Project translates directionally into Builder Project, preserving mutable next-release workspace meaning and distinctions from Release Cut/Product/Install/Artifact, while narrowing configuration. Installed builder Product may be substrate. SPEC retains source ownership; World Model owns target only. Any concept/context/basis/configuration-relation/scope change invalidates translation until owner reevaluation. Governing is true because this clause explicitly declares itself the normative relation carrier.

conditions: Markov object is read as a candidate identity-bearing cut.
exceptions: The empirical program is not a prerequisite for all design work; general Design Module engineering law applies outside world-model Products.

grounding.quote:
If a Markov object is read as a candidate identity-bearing cut, then good
software boundary design should prefer:

- the smallest lawful carrier set that preserves the boundary's real authority
- subordinate payloads staying subordinate unless they carry independent
  authority
- resistance to boundary inflation, where many sensed fragments are promoted
  into peer objects without irreducible need
- strongly typed semantic boundaries so identity-bearing cuts are not left
  fuzzy, reconstructive, or controller-owned

This document does not make the empirical Markov-object program a prerequisite
for all design work. The relation runs the other way:

- `WORLD_MODEL_METHOD.md` gives one theoretical framing for why these boundary
  disciplines are sound
